rows.description: A friend asks you to sign as guarantor or start a venture on a handshake. Affection makes paperwork feel insulting, but clarity protects the friendship. Write it down, limit your exposure, and say kindly that paper is for both.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, deceit, dependence, guilt
related mind states: affection, trust

rows.description: They accuse you of breaching terms and threaten legal action. Stay calm, re-read the agreement, collect emails and proofs, respond in writing, and consider mediation. Escalating a fight in anger tends to cost more than either side expected.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: deceit, dependence, guilt, trust
related mind states: anger, calm

rows.description: You signed something unfavourable and now feel foolish. Recognise it as learning, review exit routes, seek legal advice, and negotiate an amendment if possible. Do not hide it or breach quietly and hope no one notices.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, deceit, dependence, trust
related mind states: hope, regret

rows.description: Cash is running out and you feel responsible for the team and investors. Tell the truth early, plan an orderly wind-down or pivot, and protect employees first. Hiding the numbers or overpromising makes damage larger.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, fear, gratitude, loyalty, resentment, rivalry
related mind states: guilt, detachment

rows.description: You blame your partner for the mistakes while ignoring your own. Hold a factual post-mortem: what decisions, what signals missed. Resentment left unspoken kills friendships that could survive the company.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, fear, gratitude, guilt, loyalty, rivalry
related mind states: resentment

rows.description: Dreading the investor update, you polish the story too much. Honest bad news given early builds trust; surprises destroy it. Ask for advice, not just money, and accept that some investors will go silent.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, gratitude, guilt, loyalty, resentment, rivalry
related mind states: fear, surprise, trust

rows.description: An investor tells you they are stepping back. It stings like abandonment, but their exit is a business choice. Thank them, ask for candid feedback and introductions, and avoid burning a bridge you may cross again.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fear, gratitude, guilt, loyalty, resentment, rivalry
related mind states: gratitude, disappointment

rows.description: Staff who stay through late salaries are giving loyalty that must not be exploited. Be transparent, pay dues first, write references, and never guilt-trip them to stay. Treat their trust as a debt to honour.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, fear, gratitude, guilt, resentment, rivalry
related mind states: guilt, trust

rows.description: Parents ask when you will take a safe job, having seen savings drain. Their fear is love speaking. Share your plan and a clear deadline, and acknowledge that risk falls on them too, not just on you.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, gratitude, guilt, loyalty, resentment, rivalry
related mind states: affection, fear, anxiety, trust

rows.description: Failure feels like public exposure, and you scroll through peers' funding news. Mature action: separate the company from your worth, write down lessons, tell your story honestly, and rest before deciding what next.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, fear, gratitude, guilt, loyalty, resentment
related mind states: shame
